title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Ask favours and permission politely, make and respond to invitations and offers, and refuse gracefully.
intro: Politeness in Tamil comes less from 'please' and 'thank you' than from **verb forms** and **softeners**: the -ங்க ending, the word கொஞ்சம் 'a little', questions like **'would you do…?'** (-றீங்களா?) and **'is it possible?'** (முடியுமா?), and respectful pronouns like அவங்க. Hospitality is a serious matter: guests are treated like gods (விருந்தோம்பல், the ancient virtue of hospitality).

vocab.note: spoken mostly உதவி பண்ணு / ஹெல்ப் பண்ணு

vocab.en: freely; by all means, go ahead

phrases.en: Could you keep an eye on this bag for a moment?
Would you lend me your phone for a minute?
No trouble at all — by all means.
Come to our house for a meal on Sunday.
I'll certainly come. Thank you for inviting me.
No thanks, that's enough. Thank you very much.
I'm sorry, I can't come that day.

grammar.title: Softening requests: -றீங்களா?, முடியுமா?, -ங்களேன்
grammar.body:
A bare polite imperative (குடுங்க 'give') is fine for routine requests, but for **favours**, Tamils turn the request into a **question**:

**Present tense + -ஆ?** — 'Will you…?': குடுக்கிறீங்களா? 'would you give…?', உதவி பண்றீங்களா? 'would you help?'
**Infinitive + முடியுமா?** — 'Is it possible to…?': சொல்ல முடியுமா? 'could you tell me?'
**Imperative + -ஏன்** — a gentle urging 'do…, won't you': சாப்பிடுங்களேன் 'do eat', உக்காருங்களேன் 'do sit down'

Add **கொஞ்சம்** 'a little' to almost any request to make it softer. Using the plural **-ங்க** and respectful pronouns (நீங்க, அவங்க) is itself the main politeness device.

examples.en: Would you open the door, please?
Could you tell me the way to the station?
Would you do this for me?

grammar.title: Asking permission and offering: -லாமா? and -ட்டுமா?
grammar.body:
**-லாமா?** *-lāmā?* (written -கலாமா?) asks **permission**: 'may I / may we?' — உள்ள வரலாமா? 'may I come in?', போட்டோ எடுக்கலாமா? 'may I take a photo?'. The answer is often **தாராளமா** 'by all means' or **வேணாம்** 'please don't'.

**-ட்டுமா?** *-ṭṭumā?* (the optative/hortative) **offers** to do something or asks 'shall I?': நான் உதவி பண்ணட்டுமா? 'shall I help?', கதவைச் சாத்தட்டுமா? 'shall I close the door?'. Without -ஆ it expresses 'let…': அவன் வரட்டும் 'let him come'.

Formal written Tamil also has an **optative** in -க (வாழ்க 'long live!', வருக 'welcome!') which you'll see on banners and signs.

examples.en: May I talk on the phone here?
Shall I go now? (polite way to take leave)
Let him come, then we'll eat.

dialogue.title: Visiting a friend's family
dialogue.setting: Sarah visits Meena's family home for the first time. Meena's mother greets her.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: Welcome, dear, welcome! Come in, sit down.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: வணக்கம் அம்மா. இது உங்களுக்கு ஒரு சின்ன பரிசு.
lines.roman: vaṇakkam ammā. idu ungaḷukku oru sinna parisu.
lines.en: Hello, auntie. This is a small gift for you.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: Oh, why all this? Thank you so much, dear.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Please don't go to any trouble, auntie.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: What trouble? I'll bring it right away.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: No, dear, you're the guest. Do sit down.

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.native: அம்மா, சாரா இன்னைக்கு ராத்திரி சாப்பிட்டுட்டுப் போகலாமா?
lines.roman: ammā, Sārā innaikku rāttiri sāppiṭṭuṭṭup pōgalāmā?
lines.en: Mum, can Sarah stay for dinner tonight?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: Of course! You mustn't leave without eating!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: All right, auntie, I'd be delighted.

culture: Tamil hosts will offer food and drink several times; it's polite to refuse lightly once and accept on the second offer. When you leave, say போயிட்டு வர்றேன் or ask போகட்டுமா? 'shall I go?' rather than just announcing you're leaving. Touching the feet of elders (காலில் விழு) to receive their blessing is common at weddings and festivals. Gifts are given and received with the right hand (or both hands).

tip.title: Turn the request into a question
tip.body:
- **குடுங்க** 'give' is fine for routine things. For a favour, ask a question instead.
- Present tense + **-ஆ?**: குடுக்கி**றீங்களா?** 'would you give…?', பேசு**றீங்களா?**
- Or infinitive + **முடியுமா?**: சொல்ல **முடியுமா?** 'could you tell me?'.
- Add **கொஞ்சம்** 'a little' to soften any request.

sentences.en: Would you close the window, please?
Could you speak a little more slowly?
Would you help me lift this bag?
Would you take a photo of us?
Could you help me a bit?
Could you tell me where the temple is?
Am I bothering you?
No, it's no trouble at all.
Thanks so much, that's a big help.

tip.title: May I: -லாமா? · Shall I: -ட்டுமா?
tip.body:
- **-லாமா?** asks permission: ஜன்னலைத் திறக்**கலாமா?** 'may I open the window?'.
- **-ட்டுமா?** offers: காபி கொண்டு வர**ட்டுமா?** 'shall I bring coffee?'.
- Without -ஆ it means 'let…': அவங்க தூங்க**ட்டும்** 'let her sleep'.
- The friendly yes is **தாராளமா** 'by all means'.

sentences.en: May I open the window?
May I park my scooter here? — By all means.
Sir, may I leave a little early today?
Shall I bring you a coffee?
Shall I call an auto?
Right, shall I make a move?
Let her sleep, don't make any noise.
Photos aren't allowed here.
There's no hurry, take your time.
You should show respect to elders.

tip.title: Invitations, Tamil style
tip.body:
- Invite with **வீட்டுக்கு சாப்பிட வாங்க** 'come home for a meal'; accept with **கண்டிப்பா வர்றேன்**.
- Wedding invitations (**பத்திரிகை**) are handed over in person: a phone call alone can feel cold.
- Take a small gift: fruit or sweets.
- **வருக** 'welcome' is the formal word you'll see on banners.

sentences.native: சனிக்கிழமை எங்க வீட்டுல ஒரு சின்ன விருந்து. நீங்களும் வாங்க.
sentences.roman: sanikkiḻamai enga vīṭṭula oru sinna virundu. nīngaḷum vānga.
sentences.en: We're having a small party at home on Saturday. Do come.

sentences.native: என் தங்கச்சி கல்யாணத்துக்கு உங்களைக் கூப்பிட வந்தேன்.
sentences.roman: en tangacchi kalyāṇattukku ungaḷaik kūppiḍa vandēn.
sentences.en: I've come to invite you to my sister's wedding.
Here's the invitation.
What time should I come?
The wedding reception is at six in the evening.
What gift shall we get?
Have all the guests arrived?
Welcome, welcome! (on a banner)

tip.title: Urging kindly: -ங்களேன்
tip.body:
- A host doesn't just offer, they urge. Add **-ஏன்** to the polite command: சாப்பிடுங்க → **சாப்பிடுங்களேன்** 'do eat', இருங்க → **இருங்களேன்** 'do stay'.
- It sounds warm, not bossy.
- Guests say **போதும்** 'that's enough' at least once: expect to be served more anyway!

sentences.en: Do sit down, I'll bring some coffee.
Do have another dosa.
Do try a little of this sweet.
Do stay a bit longer.
Why don't you come too?
Please, do eat before you go.
That's enough, I've eaten a lot.
He accepted my gift.
I'll definitely come another day.

tip.title: A soft no
tip.body:
- Start with an apology: **மன்னிக்கணும்** or **மன்னிச்சுக்கோங்க**.
- Give a reason and use **முடியாது** 'I can't' rather than வர மாட்டேன் 'I won't', which sounds stubborn.
- Offer another time: **இன்னொரு நாள்**.
- When someone tells you news, react with **அப்படியா?** 'really?'.

sentences.en: Sorry, I have work tomorrow.
Sorry, I won't be in town that day.
Really? Never mind, we'll meet another day.
He refused to come.
There's no need for you to come.
Do come, without fail!
I'll certainly come.
I apologise for coming late.
No coffee for me, tea is fine.
